videos.script:
Node has two module systems. {{two}} CommonJS, with require, which Node had from the start. And ES modules, with import, which is the language's own. Your code will be one kind, and your dependencies will be both.

{{decide}} So the first question is how Node decides which kind a file is. The answer is an extension, or a line in package.json. You will see one file run three ways in three folders, and one of them warn you.

{{find}} Then where Node looks for what you named. A path is a path. A package name starts a search, up through every node_modules folder to the root of the disk.

{{cache}} Then the cache. A module runs once, however many files ask for it. That makes a singleton for free, and it makes a circle of two modules quietly hand one of them something half finished.

{{meet}} Then the places the two systems meet, and the field in package.json that decides what a package lets you import. And last, the layout of the project this course builds from lesson five on.
